46332.baliContext:
**🥐 Bakery Wholesale in Bali (From Warungs to Five-Star Patisseries)**

**Industrial segment — high volume, thin margins:**
- Every hotel breakfast buffet, Indomaret/Alfamart minimarket, and Balinese school canteen uses packaged bread and crackers
- This market is dominated by major Indonesian brands: Sari Roti (Nippon Indosari), Roma biscuits (Mayora), Khong Guan crackers
- Distribution networks for these brands are owned by established national distributors — competitive and margin-thin for new entrants

**Artisan and premium segment — the PMA opportunity:**
- **Sourdough and artisan bread**: Canggu, Seminyak, and Ubud have seen an explosion of artisan bakeries since 2020. Names like Shelter Cafe, Revolver, and dozens of others create captive demand for premium sourdough loaves, focaccia, and specialty breads
- **Croissant wholesale**: Several Bali-based patisseries have grown into wholesale suppliers, distributing croissants and viennoiserie daily to boutique hotels, coffee shops, and brunch spots
- **European-style biscuits and crackers**: Premium imported crackers (French palets Bretons, Belgian speculoos, Italian biscotti) for hotel minibars and restaurant cheese boards — this is a genuine niche with margin
- Hotel procurement: 5-star hotel patisserie teams often prefer to outsource daily production of croissants, pain au chocolat, and Danish pastries to specialist wholesale bakeries

**Key operational reality:**
- Fresh bakery wholesale is a **dawn-to-shelf** business. Production at 2am, delivery by 7am, products on hotel breakfast tables by 8am
- Shelf-life management: unsold fresh bread must be managed daily. Wastage budgeting is critical to profitability
- The cold chain requirement is real but manageable at Bali's scale — refrigerated vans serving the Seminyak-Canggu-Seminyak corridor

**Industrial bakeries in Bali:**
- Several medium-scale industrial bakeries in Denpasar supply the island's supermarket network. Wholesale distributors act as the middlemen between these factories and the retailer network

46333.baliContext: This is the most strictly regulated wholesale code relevant to Bali. The alcohol distribution market is oligopolistic — dominated by a handful of established local players (particularly for spirits and wine imports). Foreign entry at the Menengah/Besar scale realistically requires a joint venture with an established local distributor who already holds the SIUP-MB and NPPBKC. Going solo means navigating Customs, warehouse zoning approvals (alcohol warehouses have strict location restrictions), and building relationships with excise officers. 46334.baliContext:
**🥤 Non-Alcoholic Beverage Wholesale in Bali (Massive Volume Market)**

**The scale of opportunity:**
- Bali has 5,000+ registered hotels and accommodation units, hundreds of beach clubs, 8,000+ F&B establishments, dozens of large-scale music and wellness events annually
- Every one of these consumes beverages daily — soft drinks for minibar, mineral water for guestroom amenities, energy drinks for beach club bar lists, fresh juice for hotel breakfasts
- This is genuinely one of Bali's highest-volume wholesale sectors

**Market segments:**

**Mineral water (AMDK) — the daily staple:**
- Aqua (Danone), Club, Ades dominate. Distribution margins are thin but volume is enormous
- Bali's small-scale hotels often buy AMDK by the pallet from local distributors; large resorts have direct supply agreements

**Energy drinks and premium carbonates — beach club fuel:**
- Beach clubs (Finns, Atlas, Potato Head, Mrs Sippy) consume extraordinary volumes of energy drinks, Fever-Tree mixers, and premium sodas
- Red Bull, Monster, Bintang Zero, San Pellegrino are the key SKUs
- These buyers are sophisticated and demand BPOM ML-registered products — rejecting grey market imports

**Premium/functional beverages — the PMA niche:**
- Sparkling water imports (San Pellegrino, Perrier, Hildon, Gerolsteiner) for 5-star hotel restaurant tables
- Cold-brew coffee wholesale: growing café market
- Kombucha: Bali has several local producers (local brands Kombucha Lab, etc.) but also imports from Australia
- Coconut water: Bali's local coconut water (brand and fresh) consumed massively; premium packaged imports (Vita Coco) distributed via this code

**Jamu and herbal drinks:**
- Jamu wholesale (Sido Muncul, Jamu Jago brand wholesale distribution) uses this code
- Wellness tourism in Ubud drives demand for premium packaged jamu — BPOM TR registration required for traditional herbal classifications

**⚠ BPOM enforcement reality:**
- BPOM has conducted multiple raids on Canggu cafés and supermarkets selling BPOM ML-unlicensed imported beverages
- Popular items caught: imported herbal teas, Australian kombucha, craft sodas without Indonesian ML registration
- Penalties: product seizure, shop closure orders. The risk of distributing unlicensed beverages is real and immediate

**Step-by-step for a PT PMA non-alcoholic beverage wholesale distributor:**

   - **MD** (Makanan Dalam): for domestically produced beverages (local brands, locally produced kombucha)
   - **ML** (Makanan Luar): for all imported packaged beverages (Monster, San Pellegrino, Gatorade, Red Bull imported variants). **No ML = cannot legally sell in Indonesia**
   - BPOM TR (Tradisional): separate registration pathway for herbal/jamu drinks under the traditional medicine framework

46335.baliContext:
**🚬 Tobacco Wholesale in Bali (High Regulation, Consistent Demand)**

**Market reality:**
- Bali has significant tobacco consumption from both domestic residents and the 6+ million annual foreign tourists
- Indonesian domestic market is one of the world's largest: kretek (clove cigarettes) are deeply embedded in Indonesian culture — Sampoerna, Gudang Garam, Djarum are household names
- Tourist demand: European, Australian, and American tourists often seek their familiar international brands (Marlboro, Camel, Dunhill) — but import restrictions make these expensive and supply constrained

**The domestic cigarette distribution model:**
- Sampoerna, Gudang Garam, and Djarum all have established regional distribution networks in Bali; breaking into this as a new PMA distributor is extremely difficult — these brands use captive distributor agreements
- The realistic entry point for a PMA operator is **premium/specialty tobacco not covered by the major brands**: Cuban cigars, Dominican cigars, premium pipe tobacco, luxury cigar accessories

**PMA niche — Premium Cigar Distribution:**
- Bali's luxury hotel segment (COMO Uma Ubud, Four Seasons Jimbaran, Bulgari Uluwatu) have cigar lounges and humidor services requiring premium cigars
- Cuban cigars (Cohiba, Montecristo, Romeo y Julieta), Dominican cigars (Arturo Fuente, Macanudo): these require legal importation with all cukai compliance and are not well-served by existing distributors
- The high-end cigar distribution market in Bali is underdeveloped — a focused premium cigar import/wholesale operation targeting hotel cigar lounges and luxury tobacco shops is a real niche

**E-cigarette/vaping sector:**
- Vaping has grown dramatically in Indonesia, including among younger Bali expat demographics
- Vape liquid wholesale requires BPOM registration + NPPBKC + compliance with Permenkes 28/2017
- Local vape liquid producers (many are small UMKM) need wholesale distribution support

**⚠ Compliance warnings:**
- DJBC (Bea Cukai) actively raids wholesale and retail tobacco operations to detect illegal pita cukai (counterfeit or missing tax stamps). Penalties: goods seizure + criminal prosecution
- Advertising violations are increasingly enforced online — Instagram/social media posts for tobacco products are monitored
- **Strongly recommend engaging a specialized customs lawyer before establishing tobacco distribution operations**

46335.whatChanged: Direct match from KBLI 2020 (MATCH_LANGSUNG). Major post-2020 developments: (1) E-cigarette and vaping regulation has intensified — Indonesia formalized BPOM registration requirements for vape liquids under Permenkes 28/2017 framework; (2) Tobacco excise rates have increased significantly annually — cukai tembakau is now up to 57% of the retail price (Harga Pokok Penjualan) for certain product categories; (3) Plain packaging discussions have intensified at the Kemenkes level; (4) WHO FCTC pressure has led to tighter advertising enforcement including digital/social media.
46335.whatItMeans: Wholesale of tobacco and tobacco products — bulk B2B distribution of cigarettes (rokok kretek, rokok putih), cigars, cigarillos, rolling tobacco, shisha/hookah tobacco, e-cigarettes (vape devices and liquid), and other nicotine products to retailers, warungs, minimarkets, hotels, convenience stores, and duty-free outlets. This is one of Indonesia's most heavily regulated wholesale sectors, sitting at the intersection of excise tax law, health regulation, advertising restrictions, and import controls. The mandatory excise tax system (cukai) — with physical tax stamps (pita cukai) on every product — creates significant compliance infrastructure requirements for any wholesale operator.
46335.whatYouNeed:
**All scales**: Low risk (Rendah). NIB issued **automatically** (Otomatis). Authority: **OSS Pusat**.

⚠️ **NOTE: NIB is only the beginning.** Operating in tobacco wholesale requires additional mandatory registrations that are sector-specific and non-negotiable. This is a regulated sector — consult legal counsel before proceeding.

**Step-by-step for a PT PMA tobacco wholesale distributor:**
1. **PT PMA incorporation** — notary deed, AHU registration; trading sector minimum IDR 10B stated (~3–5 weeks)
2. **NIB via OSS** — register on oss.go.id, select 46335, Rendah path; auto-issued (1–3 days)
3. **NPPBKC (Nomor Pokok Pengusaha Barang Kena Cukai)** — **CRITICAL MANDATORY STEP**: registration as an excisable goods operator with DJBC (Direktorat Jenderal Bea dan Cukai / Customs and Excise). Without NPPBKC, you CANNOT legally handle tobacco products in Indonesia. Application to the nearest Kantor Bea dan Cukai — typically 2–4 weeks
4. **Pita cukai (tax stamps)** — every cigarette pack, cigar, and tobacco product sold in Indonesia must bear a valid government tax stamp. As a wholesale distributor, you receive products already bearing pita cukai from manufacturers or licensed importers. Verifying and tracking pita cukai on your inventory is a legal obligation
5. **BPOM registration for e-cigarettes/vaping liquid** — Permenkes 28/2017 requires BPOM registration for vape/e-cigarette liquid (liquid contains nicotine = regulated health product). BPOM registration number must appear on packaging
6. **Import permits for cigarettes** — imported branded cigarettes (Marlboro, Dunhill, Camel) face strict import licensing; import quota from Kemendag + SNI compliance + cukai payment on import. High tariff barriers protect domestic brands
7. **API-U** — general import license from Kemendag if importing any tobacco products
8. **Advertising compliance** — PP 109/2012 and Permenkes 109/2012 impose severe restrictions:
   - No imagery of people smoking in any advertisement
   - Ads must carry health warning (minimum 10% of ad area)
   - No advertising near schools, playgrounds, or health facilities
   - TV advertising only permitted 21:30–05:00
   - Social media tobacco advertising: highly restricted
9. **STP Distributor/Agen** (optional) — Kemendag registration
10. **Laporan kegiatan usaha** — periodic business activity reports (ongoing)

**Typical total timeline:** 4–8 weeks from PT PMA to operational (NPPBKC processing time is the bottleneck).
**Minimum PT PMA capital:** IDR 10 billion stated capital (Rp 2.5B paid-up).

**Authority:** OSS Pusat.
**PMA:** Fully open (Terbuka) — 100% foreign ownership.

47111.baliContext:
**Why is minimarket closed to foreigners?**

The explosive growth of Alfamart and Indomaret obliterated traditional warungs and small shopkeepers across Indonesia. The government's response: legally fence off small-format convenience retail (<400 sqm) for domestic UMKM and cooperatives. The policy basis is Permendag (Ministry of Trade Regulation) on modern retail, combined with Perpres 10/2021 designating this segment as UMKM-reserved. It's deliberately protective — not arbitrary.

---

**The PMA alternative: 47191 (Supermarket / Toko Modern Lainnya)**

Foreign investors wanting modern retail in Indonesia use **47191** — supermarkets, hypermarkets, branded specialty stores, premium grocery, department stores. All fully open to 100% PMA, no floor area minimum. Pepito Market, Bintang Supermarket, and international grocery chains in Bali all operate under 47191. The key distinction: 47191 has no size floor and no nationality restriction.

---

**The Bali triple lock (as of Feb 2026):**
- **Lock 1:** 0% PMA — foreigners cannot own 47111, full stop
- **Lock 2:** Governor Koster's letter (Jan 2026) requesting BKPM to close OSS for all low-risk PMA in Bali
- **Lock 3:** Instruksi Gubernur Bali No. 6/2025 — MORATORIUM on all new Toko Modern Berjejaring permits across all 9 Bali regencies/cities

The moratorium was the Governor's direct response to Alfamart/Indomaret saturation in tourist areas. Addressed to all Bupati/Walikota and DPMPTSP heads. Timeline to lift: unknown — requires a provincial Perda, which moves at bureaucratic speed.

---

**Common mistakes:**
- **Nominee structure** — using an Indonesian citizen as frontman while a foreigner controls the business. Asset seizure, deportation, criminal liability are documented outcomes in Bali
- **"Organic grocery" branding** — if customers pick products from shelves and pay at a cashier, and food/beverages dominate the inventory, OSS classifies it as 47111 regardless of what you call it
- **Franchise Alfamart/Indomaret** — the moratorium blocks ALL new chain permits, even for domestic franchisees
- **56101 (restaurant) workaround** — reclassification risk if packaged retail goods generate >50% of revenue

If you are a foreign investor wanting to enter modern retail in Indonesia, you need a different code: 47191 covers supermarkets, hypermarkets, and large-format modern retail — fully open to 100% PMA, no size restriction.

**If you are an Indonesian national or domestic entity:**

**All scales (Mikro/Kecil/Menengah/Besar):** Low risk (Rendah). NIB only — issued automatically (Otomatis) via OSS.

**Authority:** OSS Pusat (central OSS system). Note: ignore the "Gubernur Daerah Khusus Jakarta" scale entry — that is a Jakarta-specific governance anomaly and does not apply to Bali or other provinces. For all non-Jakarta operators: NIB is auto-issued via OSS Pusat.

**Step-by-step for a domestic operator:**
1. **Business entity setup** — PT or CV, notary deed, AHU registration (~1–2 weeks)
2. **NIB via OSS** — register on oss.go.id, select 47111, auto-issued (1–2 days)
3. **KKPR** — spatial conformity for commercial zoning, from ATR/BPN (required before opening)
4. **PBG** — building permit if constructing or renovating; replaces IMB (4–12 weeks)
5. **Kemitraan UMKM** — formal partnership agreement with micro/small businesses (post-licensing obligation)
6. **Annual report** to Menteri Perdagangan — business activity report

**Post-issuance obligations:**
- Comply with Toko Swalayan regulations (Permendag on modern retail)
- Active UMKM kemitraan (shelf-space or supplier agreements)
- Supply minimum domestic product quota
- Comply with operational hour limits
- Annual activity reports to Ministry of Trade

**⚠️ BALI MORATORIUM (additional block for domestic operators too):** Instruksi Gubernur Bali No. 6/2025 suspends ALL new Toko Modern Berjejaring (chain modern store) permits across Bali — PBG and NIB both blocked. Even domestic Alfamart/Indomaret franchisees cannot get new chain permits in Bali. Remains in effect until a provincial Perda is enacted.

47191.baliContext:
**47191 — the PMA retail arena in Bali**

While 47111 (minimarket) is locked for Indonesians only, 47191 is where foreign retail brands operate legally. Current examples in Bali:
- **Pepito Market** (Seminyak, Sanur, Kerobokan) — imported goods supermarket, the expat staple
- **Bintang Supermarket** (Seminyak, Kuta) — premium grocery, Bali's best-known expat chain
- **Circle K** (selected tourist areas) — international convenience chain in large-format
- International branded lifestyle stores inside Beachwalk, Discovery, and Seminyak Village malls

---

**Socio-economic study — when is it required?**

Permendag Toko Swalayan requires an analisis kondisi sosial-ekonomi (AKSE) before opening if your store will materially impact nearby traditional markets. Enforcement varies: Badung and Denpasar are stricter; Tabanan and Buleleng are more relaxed. The study assesses impact on warungs and pasar tradisional within your catchment radius. Timeline: 3–8 weeks if required. Clarify with DPMPTSP before submitting your KKPR.

---

**Mall entry: the real operational path for most PMA retailers**

For international brands, the most common route: PT PMA → mall anchor tenant agreement → NIB → store fit-out. Premium Bali mall anchor slots (Beachwalk, Discovery) run IDR 1–3 billion/year in rent. Strip-mall or stand-alone retail: IDR 200–600M/year.

---

**Common mistakes:**
- **Ignoring zoning** — KKPR is mandatory before any fit-out; Bali has strict restrictions near temples, rice paddies (subak), and coastal buffer zones
- **Operating before NIB** — even with automatic issuance, you must have the NIB document before trading
- **UMKM partnership as box-ticking** — enforcement is increasing; documented shelf-space agreements or supplier contracts are required, not just a signed letter

47721.baliContext:
**The Apoteker shortage in Bali**

Bali has approximately 350 licensed Apotekers for ~4M population — a chronic shortage that makes APA recruitment the single hardest part of opening an Apotek in Bali. Strategies used by operators:

- **Salary premium:** Bali APA market rate is IDR 7–12M/month; PMA pharmacies typically offer IDR 12–18M plus performance bonuses to compete with chain pharmacy salaries
- **Apoteker Pendamping (deputy pharmacist):** Not a workaround for the APA requirement, but you can have one APA covering primary hours and an Apoteker Pendamping covering evenings/weekends
- **University partnership:** Udayana University's Faculty of Pharmacy has placement programs; some operators sponsor final-year students as future employees (SIPA obtained post-graduation)

---

**PMA pharmacy chains operating in Bali:**
Watson's (46+ locations across Indonesia, Beachwalk mall), Guardian (part of Dairy Farm International), Century Healthcare — all operate under 47721. They employ full APA rosters and have standardized store formats that pass Dinas Kesehatan inspection on first visit.

---

**Practical advice:**
- Do not sign your lease before securing your APA. Premises without a confirmed APA cannot obtain SS — you will pay rent for months while waiting
- **Cold-chain storage** is mandatory for specific medications (insulin, certain vaccines); verify your premises can achieve 2–8°C storage before construction
- Ubud and Canggu markets: wellness-oriented positioning (herbal medicines, vitamins alongside prescription drugs) allows premium pricing; the APA barrier to entry keeps competition low

47721.whatItMeans: Apotek — full pharmacy with prescription dispensing rights. This is the most heavily regulated retail code in the 47xxx range. An Apotek holds one critical privilege no other retail type has: it can legally dispense prescription drugs (obat keras, obat etis) and prepare galenical compounded medications. The hard line: if you want to sell any medication that requires a doctor's prescription, you are an Apotek (47721), not a Toko Obat (47722). This distinction is enforced — operating without the correct license category exposes you to Kemenkes sanctions and criminal liability under UU Kesehatan.
47721.whatYouNeed:
**All scales (Mikro/Kecil/Menengah/Besar):** Risk: Menengah Tinggi (Medium-High). NIB + Sertifikat Standar (SS) — the SS is issued by Bupati/Walikota and requires physical inspection of your premises.

**Authority:** Bupati/Walikota (district/city head). In Bali: Bupati Badung for Canggu/Seminyak/Nusa Dua/Jimbaran; Walikota Denpasar for Denpasar; Bupati Gianyar for Ubud.

**Timeline:** 9 working days after physical inspection (fiktif positif applies — if no response after 9 days, the SS is deemed issued).

**PMA:** Terbuka — 100% foreign ownership allowed.

**The APA requirement — the critical constraint:**

The single biggest practical barrier to opening an Apotek is the **Apoteker Pengelola Apotek (APA)** — the responsible pharmacist who must:
- Hold a valid **STRA** (Surat Tanda Registrasi Apoteker — national pharmacist registration)
- Hold a valid **SIPA** (Surat Izin Praktek Apoteker — local practice license, issued by Dinas Kesehatan Kabupaten/Kota)
- Be physically present during pharmacy operating hours (or have a substitute Apoteker Pendamping during their absence)

The SIPA is specific to location — an Apoteker licensed for Denpasar cannot serve as APA for a pharmacy in Badung without separate approval. Without a confirmed APA with valid SIPA, your SS application will not proceed.

**Step-by-step for a PT PMA pharmacy:**
1. **PT PMA incorporation** — notary, AHU registration, capital IDR 10B minimum recommended (~3 weeks)
2. **Secure a licensed Apoteker Pengelola Apotek (APA)** — employment contract or partnership agreement; verify their STRA is current and not suspended; they must apply for local SIPA from Dinas Kesehatan Kabupaten/Kota before your SS application moves (~2–6 weeks for SIPA)
3. **Premises inspection readiness** — set up pharmacy layout per Standar Usaha Apotek: dedicated dispensing counter, cold-chain storage for temperature-sensitive medications, separate prescription and OTC sections, controlled substances cabinet (if applicable)
4. **NIB via OSS** — register on oss.go.id, select 47721, Menengah Tinggi path
5. **SS application** — OSS routes to Bupati/Walikota via DPMPTSP; attach: APA STRA + SIPA, premises layout plan, equipment inventory, PT PMA deed
6. **Physical inspection** — DPMPTSP + Dinas Kesehatan joint inspection of premises; they verify APA presence, storage standards, equipment calibration records (~1–3 weeks for scheduling)
7. **SS issuance** — within 9 working days of inspection (or fiktif positif)
8. **Total timeline:** 2–4 months from company setup to operational SS (APA recruitment is the critical path variable)

**Post-issuance obligations:**
- APA must remain in active employment (SS void if APA leaves without immediate replacement)
- Biennial review by Dinas Kesehatan
- Controlled substance reporting (if applicable)
- Periodic activity reports to Kemenkes

47722.baliContext:
**The wellness retail opportunity in Bali**

Bali's health and wellness market is one of the fastest-growing segments in the Canggu-Ubud-Seminyak corridor. 47722 is the operational license behind the health supplement stores, natural remedy shops, and holistic wellness boutiques that have proliferated since 2022.

Common 47722 business models in Bali:
- **Supplement + vitamin stores** — targeting expat and digital nomad health-conscious consumers (Canggu, Seminyak)
- **Jamu + herbal remedy shops** — traditional Indonesian medicine combined with modern packaging; popular in Ubud
- **Health product hybrid stores** — combining 47722 (OTC meds/supplements) + 47724 (cosmetics) + 47774 (essential oils/aromatherapy) under one license package

---

**TTK vs. Apoteker — the practical decision:**

If your business model is OTC + supplements only, **do not over-license**. A 47722 + TTK is faster, cheaper, and has lighter post-licensing obligations. Upgrade to 47721 (Apotek) only if you want to add prescription drug dispensing — that adds APA requirement, premises inspection, and 2x the staffing cost.

---

**OTC boundary enforcement:**

Dinas Kesehatan inspectors in Bali conduct periodic sweeps of health stores. Selling obat keras (prescription-only drugs — antibiotics, steroids, controlled substances) at a Toko Obat = immediate license suspension + criminal referral. Train your TTK on the OTC boundary, and maintain a strict stock management protocol.

47722.whatItMeans: Toko Obat — drug store selling OTC (over-the-counter) medications only. No prescription drugs, no galenical compounding. Think: paracetamol, antacids, cough syrup, vitamins, supplements, herbal remedies (jamu), plasters, bandages. The defining rule: anything that a patient can legally buy without a doctor's prescription — a Toko Obat can sell it. Anything requiring a prescription — only an Apotek (47721) can dispense. This distinction is regulated under UU Kesehatan and enforced by Dinas Kesehatan.
47722.whatYouNeed:
**All scales (Mikro/Kecil/Menengah/Besar):** Risk: Menengah Rendah (Medium-Low). NIB + Sertifikat Standar (SS) — issued automatically (Otomatis) by Bupati/Walikota via OSS.

**Authority:** Bupati/Walikota (district/city head). In Bali: Bupati Badung, Bupati Gianyar, Walikota Denpasar, etc. depending on location.

**Timeline:** Otomatis — automatic issuance, no physical inspection required for initial SS.

**PMA:** Terbuka — 100% foreign ownership allowed.

**The TTK requirement — the key staff credential:**

A Toko Obat must have a **Tenaga Teknis Kefarmasian (TTK)** — a Pharmaceutical Technical Personnel. A TTK is:
- A graduate of a Diploma III or Diploma IV pharmacy program (D3/D4 Farmasi or Analis Farmasi)
- Registered with local Dinas Kesehatan (holds STRTTK — Surat Tanda Registrasi Tenaga Teknis Kefarmasian)
- NOT the same as a full Apoteker (S1 Farmasi + Profesi); significantly easier to recruit and less expensive

A TTK earns IDR 3.5–5M/month in Bali — compared to IDR 7–12M for an Apoteker. This is the primary reason Toko Obat has a lower operational cost than Apotek.

**Step-by-step for a PT PMA Toko Obat:**
1. **PT PMA incorporation** — notary deed, AHU registration (~2–3 weeks)
2. **Recruit TTK** — confirm they hold valid STRTTK; employment contract before SS application
3. **NIB via OSS** — register on oss.go.id, select 47722, Menengah Rendah path
4. **SS application** — OSS routes to Bupati/Walikota DPMPTSP; attach: TTK credentials, premises address, company deed
5. **Automatic SS issuance** — no physical inspection for initial issuance (Otomatis); Dinas Kesehatan may conduct spot-checks post-opening
6. **Total timeline:** 3–6 weeks from company setup to trading license

**Post-issuance obligations:**
- TTK must remain in active employment (SS void if TTK departs without replacement)
- OTC-only stock enforcement — inspectors will suspend license if prescription drugs are found
- Periodic activity reports to Dinas Kesehatan

47725.baliContext:
**Why medical device retail matters in Bali**

Bali's expanding medical tourism corridor (Sanur-Denpasar-Ubud) has created genuine demand for:
- **Home healthcare equipment** for long-stay expats and retirees (blood pressure monitors, glucometers, nebulizers, mobility aids)
- **Sports medicine/rehabilitation devices** (braces, compression gear, physiotherapy equipment) for the active expat and digital nomad demographic
- **Clinic supply** — smaller clinics in tourist areas sometimes source consumables and non-critical devices from retail stores rather than wholesale PAK channels

**Current market reality:**
Bali has relatively few specialist medical device retailers. Guardian and Watson's pharmacies carry limited ranges. The gap between clinic supply and retail consumer demand is underserved — a genuine business opportunity.

---

**The izin edar in practice:**

The hardest part of this business is not the SS license — it's ensuring your entire catalog has valid Kemenkes izin edar. Common categories:
- **Blood pressure monitors, glucometers, thermometers** — most major brands (Omron, Accu-Chek, Beurer) have registered izin edar through Indonesian distributors
- **Mobility aids (wheelchairs, crutches)** — patchy coverage; generic unbranded imports often lack izin edar
- **Cosmetic devices (facial massagers, LED therapy devices)** — regulated as Alat Kesehatan Rumah Tangga Kelas 1 — require izin edar but classification is easier than medical-grade devices

**PMA strategy:**
Most PMA entrants take the **retail-from-PAK** path: source products from licensed Penyalur Alat Kesehatan (PAK) who already hold the izin edar, rather than importing and registering devices directly. This trades gross margin for speed-to-market. Once volume grows, direct import + own izin edar registration becomes economically justified.

47725.whatChanged: New KBLI 2025 code — did not exist in KBLI 2020. Previously, medical device retail may have been classified under general retail or pharmaceutical retail. PP28/2025 creates this as a distinct, dedicated classification requiring specific SS.
47725.whatItMeans: Retail sale of medical devices and health equipment — the license for stores selling blood pressure monitors, glucometers, wheelchairs, crutches, hospital beds, nebulizers, surgical instruments, and other alat kesehatan. **Every single product you sell must hold a valid izin edar (market authorization) from the Ministry of Health (Kemenkes).** The izin edar is product-specific, not store-specific — your store license (SS) covers the right to operate; the izin edar covers the right to sell each individual device. Foreign investors in Bali's health tech and medical tourism supply chain often miss this two-layer requirement.
47725.whatYouNeed:
**All scales (Mikro/Kecil/Menengah/Besar):** Risk: Menengah Rendah (Medium-Low). NIB + Sertifikat Standar (SS) — automatic issuance (Otomatis) by Bupati/Walikota via OSS.

**Authority:** Bupati/Walikota (district/city head).

**Timeline:** Otomatis — automatic SS issuance, no initial physical inspection.

**PMA:** Terbuka — 100% foreign ownership allowed.

**The izin edar requirement — the product-level gate:**

Every medical device sold in your store needs its own **izin edar alat kesehatan** from Kemenkes (Direktorat Jenderal Kefarmasian dan Alat Kesehatan). Without it, the device cannot legally be sold in Indonesia — even if your store license (SS 47725) is valid. This is not optional and not grandfathered.

How to verify: check the national SIHALKES database (regalkes.kemkes.go.id). Every legitimate medical device should show a registered izin edar with SKU, manufacturer, and importer details.

**Step-by-step for a PT PMA medical device retail store:**
1. **PT PMA incorporation** — notary deed, AHU registration (~2–3 weeks)
2. **Curate your product catalog** — before applying for SS, confirm every product has a valid Kemenkes izin edar; products without izin edar cannot be stocked
3. **For imported devices you distribute yourself:** apply for API-U (Angka Pengenal Importir Umum) and obtain izin edar through PAK (Penyalur Alat Kesehatan) registration — this process takes 3–12 months per product category
4. **For products already distributed by licensed PAK:** source from a registered Penyalur Alat Kesehatan who holds the izin edar; your role is retail only
5. **NIB via OSS** — register on oss.go.id, select 47725, Menengah Rendah path
6. **SS application** — OSS routes to Bupati/Walikota DPMPTSP; Otomatis issuance
7. **Total timeline:** 3–5 weeks for store licensing; product izin edar procurement is the long-lead item (outsource by buying from licensed PAK to avoid this)

**Post-issuance obligations:**
- Only sell products with valid izin edar — inspectors cross-reference SIHALKES
- Maintain procurement records showing izin edar numbers
- Report product incidents/complaints to Kemenkes
- Periodic reports to Dinas Kesehatan

47729.baliContext:
**🧪 Pharma Raw Materials in Bali (Niche Reality)**
- This is a small, specialized market concentrated in Denpasar and Sanur where clinics, compounding pharmacies, and aesthetic medicine practices are located
- Most demand comes from: compounding pharmacies (racikan resep), aesthetic clinics sourcing cosmeceutical actives, veterinary compounders, and research institutions (Universitas Udayana)
- Volume play is limited in Bali; the real Indonesian pharma raw materials market is in Jakarta, Surabaya, and Bandung near manufacturing clusters

---

**🎯 Where PMA Adds Genuine Value**
- **Specialty API importing** — foreign pharma companies with access to European/US GMP-certified APIs that Indonesian manufacturers cannot source locally
- **Lab reagents and diagnostics** — importing high-purity reagents for clinical labs and diagnostic centers; Bali's growing medical tourism sector creates demand
- **Cosmeceutical actives** — the boundary between pharma raw materials and cosmetic actives is thin; specialty actives used in aesthetic medicine (peptides, hyaluronic acid bulk, etc.)

---

**⚠ Critical Compliance Points**
- **Apoteker is non-negotiable** — you cannot get BPOM or Kemenkes approvals without a licensed pharmacist on staff as Penanggung Jawab
- **Cold chain compliance** — many APIs require controlled temperature storage (2–8°C or 15–25°C). BPOM inspects storage facilities
- **Per-substance approval** — each new API requires a separate BPOM process. Adding a new substance mid-operation means restarting the approval cycle for that substance
- **Controlled substance list** — some APIs are narkotika/psikotropika precursors; additional BNN authorization required. Do not assume all APIs are equivalent
- **20 hari = working days** — longest business license processing time in retail. BPOM and Kemenkes clearances must come FIRST

The customer is typically a pharmaceutical manufacturer, compounding pharmacy, clinical laboratory, or research institution — not the end patient buying off a shelf.

**Mandatory regulatory approvals on top of OSS licensing:**
- **BPOM approval per substance** — every Active Pharmaceutical Ingredient requires a separate distribution authorization from BPOM. GMP documentation from the supplier, Certificate of Analysis per batch, BPOM product file submission
- **Izin from Kemenkes** — Ministry of Health permit for dealing in pharmaceutical raw materials

**Step-by-step for a PT PMA pharmaceutical raw materials retailer:**
1. **PT PMA incorporation** — notary deed, AHU registration; pharma sector minimum IDR 10B stated (~3–5 weeks)
2. **NIB via OSS** — register on oss.go.id, select 47729, Menengah Tinggi path (~3 days)

4. **Izin distribusi bahan baku farmasi** — submitted to Kemenkes; requires company profile, qualified pharmacist (Apoteker) as Penanggung Jawab, facility inspection (2–3 months)
5. **Kemenkes facility inspection** — storage facility must meet cold-chain or controlled storage requirements
6. **Izin from Bupati/Walikota via OSS** — issued within 20 working days after BPOM and Kemenkes clearance
7. **API import license** (if importing) — Kemenkes-specific import authorization per substance per year
8. **Penanggung Jawab Apoteker** — a licensed pharmacist must be formally designated; without this, no BPOM or Kemenkes approvals proceed
9. **Annual reporting** — laporan kegiatan usaha periodic to BPOM and Kemenkes

47811.baliContext:
**🚗 Bali's Car Market (Reality Check)**
- **Dominant players:** Toyota (Auto2000), Honda (Honda Prospect Motor dealers), Mitsubishi (Krama Yudha Tiga Berlian), Suzuki — all have established dealer networks across Bali
- **Market reality:** The national dealers have Bali locked up. A new PMA entering standard mass-market new car retail would face extremely stiff competition from entrenched ATPM networks
- **EV segment:** The real near-term opportunity. BYD (now assembling in Indonesia), Wuling Air EV, and Hyundai Ioniq are generating genuine demand. The EV dealership ecosystem is nascent — ATPM agreements are newer, competition is lower, and government EV incentives (PPnBM reduction, SPKLU infrastructure grants) are active
- **Luxury imports:** Mercedes-Benz, BMW, Porsche, Audi serve the high-net-worth expat and local entrepreneur market. Bali has limited dedicated luxury car showrooms outside Denpasar — Canggu and Seminyak's expat density creates underserved demand

---

**⚠ Practical Traps**
- **The ATPM bottleneck:** Getting a genuine new car dealer agreement with a major ATPM as a new PMA is hard. Japanese brands have closed their Bali dealer networks — you'd need to acquire an existing dealership or find a brand without full Bali coverage
- **CBU vs CKD imports:** Completely Built-Up (CBU) imported cars face 50–80% import duties + 10% PPnBM; CKD assembled locally are far cheaper. PMA luxury car importers must price CBU units accordingly
- **EV infrastructure obligation:** If you sell EVs, customers increasingly expect charging at the showroom or through a network you can refer them to

**Scale-dependent licensing in PP 28/2025:**

**Kecil (Small — local dealer):** Low risk (Rendah). NIB issued **automatically** (Otomatis). Authority: **Bupati/Walikota**.
**Besar (Large — national chain):** Low risk (Rendah). NIB issued **automatically** (Otomatis). Authority: **OSS Pusat**.

Both scales require only an NIB — no Sertifikat Standar, no Izin, no separate approval. The licensing burden is genuinely low.

**The real operational requirements come from manufacturers and vehicle registration law:**

**Step-by-step for a PT PMA new car dealership:**
1. **PT PMA incorporation** — notary deed, AHU registration; automotive retail minimum capital typically IDR 10B stated (~3–5 weeks)
2. **NIB via OSS** — register on oss.go.id, select 47811, Rendah path; auto-issued (1–3 days)

4. **Showroom setup** — location must meet manufacturer's showroom standards. KKPR check for commercial vehicle retail use
5. **STNK/BPKB dealer authorization** — establish coordination with local Samsat to process STNK and BPKB issuance on behalf of buyers
6. **SNI compliance for EV charging** — if your dealership offers EV models with charging infrastructure: SNI 8972 for SPKLU applies; coordinate with PLN for power connection
7. **Laporan kegiatan usaha** — periodic business activity reports to Kemendag (ongoing obligation)

**Typical total timeline:** 2–4 months from PT PMA to showroom-ready.

47812.baliContext:
**🚙 Bali's Used Car Market (Niche but Real)**
- Bali has an active secondhand car market driven by expatriates and long-term visitors who arrive, buy a car for 2–4 years, then leave. Toyota Rush, Toyota Avanza, Honda HR-V, and Suzuki Jimny are the most liquid used car models
- **Expat rotation cycle:** Creates a steady supply of well-maintained, relatively low-mileage vehicles entering the secondhand market every year — a genuine supply opportunity
- **Price anomaly:** Good condition secondhand vehicles in Bali often sell at a premium because expat buyers in Canggu/Seminyak are willing to pay for documented condition and hassle-free transfer
- **Platform shift:** Younger Bali residents increasingly buy secondhand through OLX, Carmudi, or Moladin. A physical lot business needs digital presence to compete

---

**⚠ BPKB Irregularities — The Single Biggest Risk**
- **Gadai BPKB (BPKB as loan collateral):** A significant portion of second-hand vehicles in Indonesia have their BPKB lodged with a bank or lender as security. Buying such a vehicle without clearing the BPKB releases means you cannot complete the ownership transfer
- **Verification:** Always check BPKB status at the issuing Samsat and contact the registered bank before purchase
- **Stolen vehicle register:** Cross-check chassis number (VIN) and engine number against the Korlantas stolen vehicle database before buying expensive units
- **Pajak mati (lapsed registration):** Vehicles with multiple years of unpaid annual road tax face progressive penalties at Samsat
- **Bali notary capacity:** BPKB balik nama in Bali is done through notary (PPAT). During peak real estate seasons, Bali notaries are backlogged — factor in 2–4 week transfer timelines

**🔧 Spare Parts in Bali (Stable Demand, Niche Imports)**
- Bali's vehicle density is among the highest in Indonesia per capita — the combination of 4+ million residents, 6+ million annual tourists (2024 figure), and a massive motorbike and rental car fleet creates persistent demand for maintenance parts
- **Core market:** Workshop supply (bengkel supply) — local workshops serving private cars, rental fleets, hotel shuttle vehicles. Fast-moving items: oil filters, air filters, brake pads, spark plugs, belts, and lubricants
- **Tourist rental fleet:** Bali's car and motorbike rental sector is estimated at 100,000+ registered vehicles

---

**🎯 PMA Opportunities in This Sector**
- **JDM (Japanese Domestic Market) parts importing:** Japanese cars dominate Bali (Toyota, Honda, Suzuki are the top 3 brands). Japanese-spec OEM and high-performance parts have a niche following among Bali's car enthusiast community and premium rental operators
- **European OEM parts:** For the growing luxury car segment (BMW, Mercedes, Porsche in Bali), access to genuine European OEM parts is a genuine gap
- **EV parts ecosystem:** As EV penetration grows in Bali, demand for EV-specific maintenance items (cabin filters, brake fluid, 12V auxiliary batteries) will grow. First-mover opportunity

---

**⚠ Practical Points**
- **SNI tires is real enforcement:** The tire SNI requirement (SNI 1811) is actively enforced. Importing tires without SNI marking means confiscation. Budget IDR 50–150M per tire model for testing and certification
- **Counterfeit parts exposure:** The Indonesian aftermarket parts market has significant counterfeit/KW product circulation. Documented supply chain protects you
- **Service + parts combo:** Most successful Bali auto parts businesses combine 47820 (retail) with 45201 (automotive repair). The service workshop drives parts consumption

47901.whatItMeans: Digital marketplace platform for retail intermediation — operating an e-commerce platform, website, or mobile app that connects third-party buyers and sellers for retail transactions, earning a commission or fee from the transaction without ever taking ownership of the goods sold. This is the Tokopedia, Shopee, Bukalapak, or Airbnb model: the platform facilitates; the individual sellers own the inventory. If your platform lists products from multiple independent vendors and earns per transaction, this is the code. Contrast: if you sell your own goods online (D2C), that is 47909.
47901.whatYouNeed:
**All scales (Micro, Small, Medium, Large)**: Low risk (Rendah). NIB issued **automatically** (Otomatis). Authority: **OSS Pusat**.

The OSS licensing is genuinely minimal — NIB only. But operating a digital platform in Indonesia requires compliance with two additional regulatory frameworks outside the standard OSS licensing system:

**Critical parallel obligation: PSE Registration at Kominfo**
- **PP 71/2019** mandates that any **Penyelenggara Sistem Elektronik (PSE)** — including e-commerce marketplace platforms — must register with the Ministry of Communication and IT (Kominfo)
- **Threshold:** Any platform processing personal data of Indonesian users must register. In practice: if you have Indonesian users and process any transaction or personal data, register
- **Consequence of non-compliance:** Kominfo has demonstrated willingness to IP-block non-compliant platforms (PayPal, Steam, Epic Games blocked July 2022). A blocked platform is a non-operating business
- PSE registration is done via pse.kominfo.go.id

**Step-by-step for a PT PMA digital marketplace platform:**
1. **PT PMA incorporation** — notary deed, AHU registration; tech/digital sector minimum capital IDR 10B stated (~3–5 weeks)
2. **NIB via OSS** — register on oss.go.id, select 47901, Rendah path; auto-issued (1–3 days)
3. **PSE registration at Kominfo** — submit via pse.kominfo.go.id; documents: company identity (NIB, akta), platform description, system architecture overview, data flow documentation. Timeline: 1–2 weeks for standard platforms
4. **Data localization compliance** — under PP 71/2019 and UU PDP 2022: user personal data of Indonesian citizens must be stored on servers within Indonesian territory, or a copy maintained domestically
5. **Data Protection Officer (DPO)** — UU PDP 2022 requires a designated DPO for platforms processing personal data at scale
6. **PB UMKU per product category** (if applicable) — if your marketplace handles regulated goods (cosmetics, food, medicines), your platform-level governance over listed products may be scrutinized
7. **Laporan kegiatan usaha** — periodic business activity reports to Kemendag
8. **OJK compliance** (if fintech features) — if your platform includes buy-now-pay-later, escrow, or payment processing beyond a standard payment gateway, OJK licensing may apply separately

**Typical total timeline:** 1–3 months from PT PMA to platform compliant.
**Minimum PT PMA capital:** IDR 10 billion stated capital (Rp 2.5B paid-up).

**Authority:** OSS Pusat.
**PMA:** Fully open (Terbuka) — 100% foreign ownership.

47909.baliContext:
**🛍 Intermediary Services in Bali (Where the Real Opportunity Is)**
- 47909 is the correct code for a cluster of Bali business models that are genuinely profitable but often misclassified:

**Villa supply procurement specialist:**
- Bali has 10,000+ active villas, many managed by professional villa management companies. The management company procures F&B supplies, linen, toiletries, maintenance materials, and decor for villa owners
- A specialized villa procurement/sourcing company (47909) earns a service fee or commission on every purchase it facilitates on behalf of villa clients
- This is distinct from wholesale distribution — you don't warehouse goods; you identify, negotiate, and coordinate procurement

**Luxury shopping concierge:**
- Bali's UHNW tourist segment (private jet arrivals, villa charters in Seminyak/Uluwatu, luxury resort guests) creates demand for personal shopping and luxury goods procurement services
- Personal shopper/concierge arranging luxury items (watches, bags, jewelry, bespoke garments) for wealthy visitors — earning commission or retainer fees

**Corporate procurement aggregator:**
- Aggregating purchasing needs of multiple hotel groups or F&B operators and negotiating bulk pricing with suppliers — earning an aggregation/coordination fee

---

**⚠ Know When 47909 Ends and Other Codes Begin**
- **47901 (digital marketplace):** If you build a platform where third parties transact, that's 47901. 47909 is for human-mediated intermediary service, not automated platform facilitation
- **46100 (wholesale agents/brokers):** If you intermediate wholesale (B2B, volume) transactions — buyer is a business, not a consumer — that's 46100, not 47909
- **MLM/network marketing:** If your business recruits distributors who recruit distributors (downline structure), Kemendag scrutiny is real; enforcement of Permendag 70/2019 has intensified
- **Scale threshold:** In practice, a standard service-fee intermediary (concierge, buying agent) stays Rendah regardless of revenue. The Tinggi path is specifically activated by the MLM/direct-selling structure, not by business size alone

49213.baliContext:
**🚌 Bali Transport: The Real PMA Opportunity**
- The mass ride-hailing market (Gojek, Grab) is UMKM territory — PMA cannot operate a competing app
- The actual PMA opportunity is in **organized charter and shuttle operations** serving the tourism economy

**High-demand corridors (2025):**
- **Airport–Canggu / Airport–Seminyak:** Kuta taxis still dominate but corporate shuttle contracts for hotels are underserved
- **Denpasar–Ubud:** One of the most traveled tourist routes; no quality scheduled service with Western UX exists
- **Resort shuttle circuits:** Large Nusa Dua and Uluwatu resorts pay IDR 2–4M/day for dedicated charter vehicles
- **AKAP Bali–Surabaya / Bali–Malang:** Long-haul overnight coaches via Ketapang ferry; underserved quality tier

**EV fleet opportunity:**
- Government incentives for electric commercial vehicles (2024 Perpres 55/2019 and amendments)
- An EV shuttle fleet (Tesla vans are too expensive; Hiace/BYD electric conversions are feasible) serving premium Bali hotels is a genuine white space

**ITDP/BRT tender:**
- Bali Provincial Government has received World Bank/ITDP support for Bus Rapid Transit planning. Formal tender processes for BRT operation could open B2G opportunities for PMA transport companies

**⚠ KIR is real enforcement:**
- Dishub does conduct roadside checks in Bali, especially in peak season (July–August, December)
- Expired KIR = vehicle impounded. 6-month cycle is non-negotiable for commercial operators

49213.whatItMeans: Urban passenger transport — operating scheduled or chartered buses, minibuses, and shuttle services within and between cities. This includes: city buses and urban transit, airport shuttle services, resort/hotel charter transfers, and inter-city regular routes (AKDP — Antar Kota Dalam Provinsi). The code covers the vehicle operation business itself, whether scheduled (trayek) or unscheduled (non-trayek) charter. Critical PMA distinction: the ride-hailing app model (Gojek, Grab, InDriver for ride orders via app) is explicitly reserved for Indonesian MSMEs and cannot be operated by a PT PMA. The PMA-accessible opportunity is the transport operation itself — charter fleets, shuttle services, hotel/resort transfers, and formal bus routes.

**All scales**: Low risk (Rendah). NIB issued **automatically** (Otomatis). Authority: **Bupati/Walikota**.

The NIB is auto-issued, but actual operations require additional transport-specific permits:

**Step-by-step for a PT PMA urban/charter transport operator:**
1. **PT PMA incorporation** — notary deed, AHU registration; transport sector minimum IDR 10B stated (~3–5 weeks)
2. **NIB via OSS** — register on oss.go.id, select 49213, Rendah path; auto-issued (1–3 days)
3. **Izin Usaha Angkutan** — operational transport license from Dinas Perhubungan Kabupaten/Kota; requires vehicle list (STNK), driver credentials, operational base (pool/garasi)
4. **Izin Trayek** (for fixed routes) — route permit from Dishub if operating scheduled routes between specific points. Bali routes (Denpasar–Ubud, Denpasar–Canggu, airport shuttles) require route-specific permits
5. **KIR (Uji Berkala Kendaraan Bermotor)** — roadworthiness test mandatory every **6 months** for all commercial passenger vehicles. Performed at Dishub balai uji; vehicles without valid KIR cannot legally operate
6. **STNK atas nama PT** — all fleet vehicles must be registered under the PT PMA name
7. **Asuransi Jasa Raharja** — mandatory passenger liability insurance (automatically included for registered vehicles)
8. **Driver AKAP/AKDP competency** — drivers on inter-city routes require specific Dishub certification
9. **Laporan operasi berkala** — periodic operational reports to Dishub

**For AKAP routes (inter-provincial, e.g. Bali to Java):**
- Additional **Izin Usaha Angkutan AKAP** from Kementerian Perhubungan (Menteri level)
- Bali–Java ferry coordination (ASDP Indonesia Ferry) for Bali–Ketapang (Banyuwangi) crossing

49231.baliContext:
**🚛 Road Freight in Bali (Stable B2B Market)**
- Bali's logistics market is entirely B2B-driven: there is no large-scale consumer parcel delivery market (that's dominated by JNE/J&T/SiCepat through national networks)
- The real opportunity is **dedicated B2B supply chain** serving Bali's hospitality and construction sectors

**Hotel and resort supply chain:**
- Bali has 4,000+ hotels and 10,000+ villas — each requiring daily/weekly deliveries of F&B supplies, linen, amenities, and maintenance materials
- Most large resort groups (Marriott, Hilton, Accor) source from Java-based suppliers; last-mile from Ketapang ferry port to the resort is frequently unreliable
- A dedicated 3PL (third-party logistics) company with reliable trucks, temperature-aware dry storage, and hotel-trained drivers is genuinely underserved

**Construction haulage:**
- Bali's ongoing construction boom (villas, hotels, roads) requires constant movement of building materials. Sand, gravel, steel, and prefab elements from Java via Ketapang are a steady revenue stream

**Bali–Java corridor:**
- The ASDP ferry (Ketapang–Gilimanuk) is the chokepoint for all surface freight in and out of Bali
- Ferry capacity is limited; peak season (July–August, December) creates severe backlogs
- A company with pre-booked ferry slots (via ASDP account) has a significant operational advantage

**⚠ KIR every 6 months — operational discipline required**
- KIR is not a one-time step. Every commercial vehicle has its own 6-month KIR expiry cycle
- With a fleet of 10 trucks, you're managing 10 separate KIR schedules
- Fleet management software or a dedicated compliance coordinator is essential
- Dishub does conduct spot checks on major roads (bypass Ngurah Rai, Sunset Road, etc.)

49231.whatChanged: Direct match from KBLI 2020 (MATCH_LANGSUNG). General road freight is a stable, consistently regulated category. PP 28/2025 formalizes the OSS pathway; KIR and SNI compliance requirements are governed by UU LLAJ 22/2009 and BSNI standards respectively, both predating this regulation.
49231.whatItMeans: General cargo road freight — operating trucks and commercial vehicles to transport non-specialized goods by road for third-party clients. This covers: trucking companies, last-mile delivery for B2B clients, hotel and resort supply chain distribution, construction materials haulage, and general merchandise distribution. The defining characteristic is 'barang umum' (general goods) — contrast with 49239 which covers specialized cargo (liquids, hazardous materials, refrigerated goods, heavy equipment). If you move general dry goods by road for payment, this is the code.
49231.whatYouNeed:
**Scale-dependent licensing in PP 28/2025:**

**Kecil (Small fleet):** Medium-Low risk (Menengah Rendah). NIB + Sertifikat Standar. Authority: **Bupati/Walikota**. Processing: **7 working days**.
**Besar (Large fleet / inter-provincial):** Medium-Low risk (Menengah Rendah). NIB + Sertifikat Standar. Authority: **Menteri** (Kementerian Perhubungan). Processing: **7 working days**.

**Step-by-step for a PT PMA general freight operator:**
1. **PT PMA incorporation** — notary deed, AHU registration; logistics sector minimum IDR 10B stated (~3–5 weeks)
2. **NIB via OSS** — register on oss.go.id, select 49231, Menengah Rendah path (~3 days)
3. **Izin Usaha Angkutan Barang** — freight transport business license from Dinas Perhubungan Kabupaten/Kota (Kecil) or Kementerian Perhubungan (Besar); documents: STNK fleet list, garansi pool address, NPWP
4. **KIR (Uji Berkala Kendaraan Bermotor)** — mandatory vehicle roadworthiness test every **6 months** for all commercial freight vehicles. This is an ongoing operational compliance item — each vehicle has its own KIR schedule. Expired KIR = vehicle cannot legally haul cargo
5. **SNI marking verification** — commercial vehicles must use SNI-compliant tires (SNI 1811), brakes, and structural components. When purchasing trucks, verify SNI compliance on key components before putting vehicles into commercial service
6. **Surat Jalan** — cargo manifest / delivery letter required for every shipment, documenting origin, destination, cargo type, weight, and vehicle details
7. **STNK atas nama PT** — fleet vehicles registered under PT PMA
8. **AKAP barang permit** (if crossing provincial borders) — inter-provincial freight requires additional Izin Usaha Angkutan Barang AKAP from Kementerian Perhubungan. Bali–Java crossings (via Ketapang ferry) require this
9. **Asuransi kargo** — cargo insurance per shipment; required by most B2B clients
10. **Laporan kegiatan usaha** — periodic operational reports (ongoing obligation)

**Typical total timeline:** 2–4 months from PT PMA to operational fleet.
**Minimum PT PMA capital:** IDR 10 billion stated capital (Rp 2.5B paid-up).

52292.baliContext:
**📦 Bali's Warehousing Gap (Real Market Opportunity)**
- Bali has a significant deficit of modern, Class A warehousing. The island has traditionally relied on Java-based warehousing, with goods shipped across the Ketapang–Gilimanuk strait to order
- **Why this matters:** Bali's 4,000+ hotels, 10,000+ villas, and hundreds of restaurants place daily orders for F&B supplies, amenities, cleaning products, and linens — most of which are sourced from Surabaya or Jakarta distributors
- A local 3PL operator with quality dry storage, reliable inventory management software, and hotel-experienced staff can command premium contract rates

**The hotel supply chain model:**
- A resort paying IDR 50–150M/month for F&B supply chain services is not unusual for a 5-star property
- Consolidating supply for 10–20 hotels into a single warehouse cuts their per-hotel logistics cost by 30–40%
- Adding a Gudang Berikat function (bonded warehouse) allows hotel clients to defer import duty on wine, spirits, and luxury food imports — a major selling point

**Strategic zone: Mengwi / Mambal / Pesiapan**
- These Kabupaten Badung industrial zones have the best access to the airport, Kuta/Seminyak hotel corridor, and the Denpasar port
- Land lease rates (Hak Sewa): IDR 200–500M/year for 1,000–2,000m² warehouse
- Industrial zone pre-zoning means KKPR is streamlined

**Combined model:**
- **52292 (dry) + 52291 (cold/refrigerated)** — full-service logistics for hotels requiring ambient-stored F&B (dry goods, packaged) and temperature-controlled goods (fresh produce, dairy, meat) in the same facility

**⚠ Laporan stok is real compliance:**
- If you store government-regulated commodities (beras/rice, gula/sugar, minyak goreng/cooking oil, tepung), monthly stock reports to Disperindag are mandatory
- Non-reporting can trigger warehouse inspection and temporary suspension of Izin Gudang

52292.whatChanged: Direct match from KBLI 2020 (MATCH_LANGSUNG). Non-refrigerated warehousing is a stable category. PP 28/2025 formalizes the OSS pathway; the IMB→PBG transition (2021) is the most significant procedural change, replacing the old IMB with the new PBG framework.
52292.whatItMeans: Non-refrigerated warehousing and storage — operating dry goods warehouses for third-party clients, providing storage space, inventory management, and logistics handling for general merchandise that does not require controlled temperature. This covers: third-party logistics (3PL) warehousing, general merchandise storage, bonded warehouses (Gudang Berikat — under Bea Cukai supervision for imported goods), and supply chain storage for hotels, resorts, and retail. The defining feature: the goods don't need refrigeration. Contrast with 52291 (cold storage / refrigerated warehousing).
52292.whatYouNeed:
**Single scale in PP 28/2025 data**: Medium-High risk (Menengah Tinggi). NIB + Izin required — **not automatic**. Issued by **Bupati/Walikota** within **5 working days**.

**Step-by-step for a PT PMA non-refrigerated warehouse operator:**
1. **PT PMA incorporation** — notary deed, AHU registration; logistics/warehousing sector minimum IDR 10B stated (~3–5 weeks)
2. **NIB via OSS** — register on oss.go.id, select 52292, Menengah Tinggi path (~3 days)
3. **IMB/PBG (Persetujuan Bangunan Gedung)** — building permit for the warehouse structure from DPMPTSP Kabupaten; documents: site plan, architectural drawings, structural calculations. New warehouses: 4–12 weeks. Existing licensed buildings: verify PBG is current
4. **KKPR** (Kesesuaian Kegiatan Pemanfaatan Ruang) — spatial/zoning conformity; warehouse must be in an area zoned for industrial/logistics use. Kawasan industri (Mengwi, Mambal, Pesiapan) are pre-zoned; greenfield sites outside industrial zones require KKPR check
5. **Izin Gudang** — warehouse operating license from Dinas Perindustrian dan Perdagangan (Disperindag) Kabupaten; documents: PBG, SKMHT (building ownership), company profile, floor plan
6. **Izin from Bupati/Walikota via OSS** — issued within 5 working days after IMB/PBG and Izin Gudang clearance
7. **Laporan stok berkala** — mandatory monthly stock reporting to Disperindag for certain commodity categories (rice, sugar, cooking oil, and other strategically regulated goods). If you store these commodities, monthly reporting is non-negotiable
8. **Gudang Berikat license** (if storing imported goods pre-customs clearance) — from Bea Cukai; additional process but opens significant B2B opportunity
9. **Fire safety compliance** — APAR (fire extinguisher) density, hydrant system, and evacuation plan per Permenaker 04/1980; inspected by Dinas Pemadam Kebakaran
10. **Laporan kegiatan usaha** — periodic business activity reports (ongoing obligation)

**Typical total timeline:** 3–6 months from PT PMA to operational warehouse (driven primarily by PBG timeline for new construction).
**Minimum PT PMA capital:** IDR 10 billion stated capital (Rp 2.5B paid-up).

**Authority:** Bupati/Walikota.
**PMA:** Fully open (Terbuka) — 100% foreign ownership.

56102.baliContext:
**🚚 The Bali Food Truck & Market Stall Scene (2025)**

**What's working:**
- **Canggu food truck culture:** The Berawa/Batu Bolong corridor has 3–5 active food truck parks; specialty coffee trucks, Japanese-inspired street food, and gourmet burgers are common formats
- **Seminyak night markets and pop-ups:** Weekend bazaars and rooftop pop-up events rotate vendors; 56102 is the legal structure for all of them
- **Beach club vendor slots:** Finns, Tropicola, and similar venues rent stall/vendor spots to external F&B operators; you need 56102 + Label HSP to legally operate in these spaces
- **Festival and event catering:** BIAF (Bali International Art Festival), Ubud Writers Festival, local festivals — the event catering market requires 56210 for contracted catering but 56102 for a stall/stand format

**PMA food truck concept — what actually works:**
- Specialty single-product concept: matcha soft serve, authentic NY-style pizza, Korean fried chicken — works when there's genuine product differentiation from local warung
- Mobile specialty coffee with roaster story: Bali's coffee culture supports premium positioning; mobile format lowers barrier vs permanent café
- Artisan ice cream with local ingredients: Kintamani coffee, Bali vanilla, salak — tourist segment pays premium for 'local + premium' positioning

**Revenue reality:**
- A well-positioned food truck/stall in Canggu or Seminyak: IDR 5–25M/day in sales (high season)
- Beach club vendor slot rent: IDR 2–5M/day site fee + % of revenue to venue
- Weekend market stall: IDR 500K–2M/day site fee; IDR 3–10M sales on strong market days

---

**⚠ Key Issues**
- **Location permit is location-specific** — Label HSP covers your unit; where you park/operate requires separate location authorization; beach/coastal sites are strictly controlled by Dinas Pariwisata and sometimes require KKPR clearance
- **Fire safety for mobile kitchens** — gas cylinder storage and ventilation in food trucks requires compliance with DAMKAR (Dinas Pemadam Kebakaran) standards; annual inspection recommended
- **No alcohol without SKPL** — even if the beach club next to you serves drinks, your truck cannot; get SKPL if your concept includes alcohol service

56102.whatChanged: Direct match from KBLI 2020 (MATCH_LANGSUNG). Code and scope unchanged — 56102 has always covered non-permanent food structures. The distinction between Label HSP (56102) and Sertifikat SLHS (56101) was clarified in PP28/2025's updated obligation framework. The food truck and pop-up culture has grown dramatically since 2020 but the legal framework is the same code.
56102.whatItMeans: Food service from non-permanent structures — food trucks, mobile warung, market stalls, pop-up food stands, and street food carts operating as a formal business entity. The defining legal characteristic is **bangunan tidak tetap** (non-permanent structure): the food preparation and serving facility is not a fixed building. If your kitchen is on wheels, in a tent, at a market kiosk, or at a temporary stall, this is your code. This is categorically different from 56101 (restaurant in a permanent building). A PT PMA running an artisan food truck concept — specialty coffee, gourmet burgers, craft ice cream, fusion street food — operates under this code.
56102.whatYouNeed:
**All scales (Mikro/Kecil/Menengah/Besar): Low Risk (Rendah)**
NIB + Sertifikat Standar issued **automatically** (Otomatis) via OSS. Authority: **Bupati/Walikota** (district/city level).

**Post-issuance obligations:**
- **Label Higiene Sanitasi Pangan (HSP)** — mandatory. This is a **label** (simpler declaration), NOT the full Sertifikat SLHS (Sertifikat Laik Higiene Sanitasi) required for permanent restaurants. Issued by Dinas Kesehatan after basic inspection; faster and lower cost than the SLHS.
- **Laporan berkala** — periodic activity reports to Bupati/Walikota
- No alcohol sales without **SKPL** (Surat Keterangan Penjualan Langsung) — food trucks are typically non-alcoholic; if you want to serve beer or wine at a pop-up, this requires a separate permit

**Note on Label HSP vs Sertifikat SLHS:**
- Label HSP = simpler food hygiene declaration for mobile/non-permanent operations; issued after a basic hygiene inspection
- Sertifikat SLHS = full health feasibility certification for permanent restaurant (56101); more complex and takes longer
- Using 56102 with Label HSP is the fast, correct path for food trucks; do not apply for SLHS if your structure is non-permanent

**Step-by-step for PT PMA food truck:**
1. **PT PMA incorporation** — notary deed, AHU registration; IDR 10B stated capital (~3–5 weeks)
2. **NIB via OSS** — select 56102; auto-issued 1–3 days
3. **Label HSP** — apply to Dinas Kesehatan kabupaten/kota; basic hygiene inspection of your mobile unit (~2–4 weeks)
4. **Operational permits for location** — depending on where you operate:
   - Public market/bazaar: letter from market management
   - Road-side: Izin Gangguan (if required by local regulation) from Satpol PP
   - Beach area: Izin from Dinas Pariwisata or Dinas Kelautan for beach/coastal zones
   - Private venue (beach club, event): venue's own permit covers you as tenant
5. **PIRT** (Produksi Industri Rumah Tangga) — if producing packaged food items (bottled sauces, packaged products) for sale alongside your truck; issued by Dinas Kesehatan separately

**Typical total timeline:** 4–8 weeks from PT PMA to operational.
**Minimum PT PMA capital:** IDR 10 billion stated capital (Rp 2.5B paid-up).

**PMA:** Fully open (Terbuka) — 100% foreign ownership.

56302.baliContext: THIS IS THE MOST DANGEROUS CODE IN BALI. Satpol PP (Public Order Enforcement) now classifies venues by operational reality, not license text. If you have a DJ booth, dance floor, and ticketed entry, you ARE 56302 regardless of what your NIB says. CRITICAL ZONING: 56302 is PROHIBITED in Yellow (Residential) and Green (Agricultural) zones. Requires specific Tourism/Entertainment Zoning. Many Canggu venues operated as 'restaurants' (56101) or 'bars' while functioning as nightclubs — these face immediate closure when audited. The SKPL alcohol license is a scarce, quota-controlled asset in saturated areas like Seminyak. Noise regulations (decibel limits) are now actively enforced with professional measurement equipment.

60103.whatChanged: CODICE_RINUMERATO from KBLI 2020 code 60102 (Private Radio Broadcasting). The name change is significant — KBLI 2025 explicitly separates on-demand streaming from traditional broadcasting, recognizing the digital shift. However, the licensing requirements inherited from broadcasting are arguably over-regulated for pure streaming services.
60103.whatItMeans: On-demand audio distribution and streaming services — music streaming, audio podcasts, audiobooks. Covers subscription-based and ad-supported models. Includes both third-party content distribution and original content. Does NOT include traditional radio broadcasting (60101/60102).
60103.whatYouNeed:
**ALL scales: High Risk (Tinggi).** NIB + full License (Izin). Processing takes up to **29 working days** (7 admin + 15 technical inspection + 7 fee verification).

Requires: broadcasting plan (background, revenue projections, shareholding structure, coverage map, facilities), board members not blacklisted, multiple sworn statements (compliance, frequency licensing, content regulation), operational feasibility test, broadcasting license fee payment within 15 days.

**Authority:** Minister / Agency Head.

**PMA:** Fully open — 100% foreign ownership allowed.
60103.youllAlsoNeed:
- 59201 — Sound Recording (for original audio production)
- 63101 — Data Processing (for streaming infrastructure)
- 73100 — Advertising (if ad-supported model)
- 62199 — Software Development (for the streaming app)
60103.zantaraOpener: Launching an audio streaming platform in Indonesia? 60103 is your code — but brace yourself for High Risk broadcasting-era licensing requirements.

60203.baliContext: Same regulatory challenges as 60103. For Bali-based video content creators, the High Risk classification is a major obstacle. Most Bali-based content creators distribute via YouTube/Instagram (platform operators bear the regulatory burden) rather than building their own streaming platforms.

60390.whatChanged: BPS_ONLY — ENTIRELY NEW code in KBLI 2025. No direct predecessor. Previously social media platforms fell under web portal codes (63122) or were unclassified. The explicit inclusion of game item marketplaces and digital voucher sales is notable — Indonesia is acknowledging the digital goods economy.
60390.whatItMeans: Social networking sites and content distribution/sharing platforms. Includes blogs, wikis, online gaming video sites, e-book distribution (non-publishing), and digital game intermediary services (vouchers, in-game items, premium access via marketplaces). A catch-all for social/sharing platforms.
60390.whatYouNeed:
**BPS_ONLY** — no PP28 risk assignment yet. Currently pending formal licensing framework. In practice, operators must register as PSE (Private Electronic System Provider) with Kominfo.

Likely will be classified as High Risk when PP28 integration occurs, given content moderation obligations.

**PMA:** Fully open — 100% foreign ownership allowed.

Running this from Bali is technically fine but unusual — the real bottleneck is BSSN registration, which requires physical infrastructure audits and Jakarta-based meetings. Most Bali-based IT companies encounter this code only when they NEED electronic certificates for their own products, not when they're issuing them.

62203.whatChanged: MATCH_CON_AGGREGAZIONE — consolidated from multiple old codes related to electronic trust services in KBLI 2020. Previously, different aspects of certificate services (issuance, management, timestamp) lived under separate codes. KBLI 2025 merges them, which simplifies licensing but means the combined code inherits the strictest requirements from all predecessors.
62203.whatItMeans: Electronic certificate services — issuing and managing digital signatures, electronic certificates, timestamp authorities, and cryptographic trust services. This is the code for Certificate Authorities (CAs), digital signature providers, and any company that issues the electronic credentials that make digital transactions legally binding in Indonesia.
62203.whatYouNeed:
**ALL scales are Medium-High risk** (Menengah Tinggi). NIB + Standard Certificate verified within **7 working days**.

Requires: org chart with qualified cryptographic/security staff, employment contracts, business process documentation, equipment inventory. Additionally, you must register with BSSN (Badan Siber dan Sandi Negara — National Cyber and Crypto Agency) as an electronic certificate provider. BSSN registration is a separate process from OSS and adds significant compliance burden — expect 2-4 months for full approval.

**PMA:** Fully open — 100% foreign ownership allowed.

64194.baliContext:
**🏦 BPR in Bali — The Microfinance Banking Layer**

**What BPR does that banks won't:**
- Provides loans of IDR 2–500 juta to UMKM operators, farmers, fishermen, village traders, and craftsmen who lack the collateral or documentation for commercial bank credit
- Accepts savings deposits from local community members (typically higher interest rate than bank savings, attracting local depositors)
- Processes faster than commercial banks — credit approval in 1–5 days vs 2–4 weeks for commercial bank SME loans

**Bali BPR landscape:**
- Bali has 130+ active BPRs (as of 2024) concentrated in Denpasar, Gianyar, Badung, and Tabanan
- Notable Bali BPRs: BPR Tish, BPR Dinar, BPR Sukawati Pancakanti (Gianyar focus), BPR Artha Hapat
- Competition is intense in south Bali; underpenetrated areas: Bangli, Karangasem (east Bali), Buleleng (north Bali)

**The 40% foreign + 60% Indonesian structure in practice:**
- Foreign investor contributes 40% equity (e.g., IDR 2.4 miliar of IDR 6 miliar minimum)
- Indonesian co-founder holds 60% (IDR 3.6 miliar) — must be a qualified individual or entity, not a nominee
- The Indonesian partner(s) must pass OJK fit & proper — no criminal record, no previous banking violations
- Common structure: experienced local Balinese banker (ex-BRI, ex-BNI) as 60% partner + foreign capital as 40% minority investor

**BPRS niche — halal microfinance for Middle Eastern tourism segment:**
- Bali receives increasing Middle Eastern and South Asian Muslim tourists
- A BPRS (Syariah) specifically serving halal-economy businesses (halal restaurants, Muslim-friendly homestays, abaya/modest fashion boutiques) = underexplored niche
- DSN-MUI sharia certification for products adds credibility

**⚠ Critical Issues**
- **40% cap is absolute** — OJK has rejected BPR applications where the foreign investor tried to exceed 40% through nominee structures; this is treated as fraud
- **Geographic restriction is real** — a Badung BPR cannot serve Ubud clients without opening a Gianyar branch (separate OJK approval); plan geographic scope from day one
- **NPL management is existential** — OJK places BPRs with NPL > 5% under enhanced supervision; NPL > 8% triggers OJK intervention; the BPR sector had 10+ forced mergers 2022–2024 due to NPL crises

64194.whatChanged: Direct match from KBLI 2020 (MATCH_LANGSUNG). BPR was significantly restructured by **UU 4/2023 (P2SK Law)** which renamed BPR to 'Bank Perekonomian Rakyat' (keeping the same BPR acronym) and expanded the BPR product scope slightly. Key change: BPRs may now offer additional savings products and certain remittance services. The 40% foreign ownership cap is unchanged. OJK transferred BPR supervision fully from BI to OJK, which was completed in 2023.
64194.whatItMeans: Bank Perkreditan Rakyat (BPR) — Indonesia's rural/community bank providing basic banking services (savings, deposits, and credit) to local communities, SMEs, and individuals in their licensed geographic area. BPR cannot offer giro (checking accounts), cannot participate in national clearing, and cannot conduct international/foreign currency transactions — these are reserved for Umum banks. This is microfinance banking, not commercial banking. **TERBATAS (limited) foreign ownership: maximum 40% foreign shareholding.** Indonesian investors must hold at least 60%. OJK issues the BPR license — this is a full bank license process, not a standard OSS procedure.
64194.whatYouNeed:
**Risk: Tinggi.** The OSS process (NIB) is the administrative layer; the **OJK bank license is the operative requirement and takes 12–24 months.**

**Foreign ownership limit: maximum 40%.** This is a TERBATAS code — not fully open to PMA. Your Indonesian partner(s) must hold at least 60% of shares and be individuals or entities with proven financial capacity (fit & proper).

**Modal minimum by geographic category (per OJK POJK 5/2015 and updates):**
- **Wilayah Jabodetabek** (Jakarta Greater Area): IDR 16 miliar
- **Ibukota Provinsi** (Provincial capital, e.g., Denpasar): IDR 8 miliar
- **Kabupaten/Kota lain** (Other cities/regencies — most of Bali): IDR 6 miliar
- The entire capital must be paid up in full at time of OJK application

**TWO-PHASE process:**

**PHASE 1 — OSS / NIB:**
- Register PT (domestic structure required, since 60% must be Indonesian) on OSS
- Select 64194, Tinggi
- NIB issued; this does NOT authorize banking operations

**PHASE 2 — OJK BPR License (12–24 months):**
1. **Principle Approval (Izin Prinsip)** — initial OJK application showing founding shareholders, business plan, location; OJK evaluates feasibility (~3–6 months)
2. **Establishment (Pendirian)** — incorporate PT after Izin Prinsip; all shareholders must pass OJK fit & proper test
3. **Capital injection** — fully paid up in escrow; evidence submitted to OJK
4. **Physical premises** — OJK inspects the proposed office location; BPR cannot operate from virtual office
5. **Core Banking System** — OJK evaluates IT infrastructure; CBS must meet OJK POJK 75/2016 standards
6. **Director/Commissioner Fit & Proper** — OJK personally vets each director and commissioner
7. **Izin Usaha OJK** — issued after all stages clear; only then can BPR open to the public
8. **OJK ongoing supervision** — monthly financial reporting; annual audit by OJK-accredited auditor; Capital Adequacy Ratio (CAR) minimum 12%; NPL must not exceed 5%

**Geographic operational limit:** BPR may only operate within its licensed province. A Bali BPR cannot open branches in Java or Lombok without separate OJK approval.

**BPRS (Syariah) variant:** BPR Syariah follows sharia finance principles; governed by OJK and DSN-MUI; same capital requirements and foreign ownership limit of 40%.

**Typical full timeline:** 18–30 months from concept to first customer.

64921.baliContext:
**🤝 The Indonesian Cooperative Landscape (Context for Foreign Investors)**

**Why this code matters to understand even if you can't use it:**
- Indonesia has 130,000+ registered cooperatives, of which ~20,000 are KSP; they collectively serve ~28 million member-borrowers
- KSP serves the UMKM segment that commercial banks won't touch: small traders, artisans, farmers, fishermen, temple offering sellers
- In Bali, the traditional Lembaga Perkreditan Desa (LPD) — Bali's unique village-level financial institution — operates alongside KSP serving the same base (LPD is actually NOT covered by KBLI 64921 — it has its own Perda Bali framework)
- The KSP sector in Indonesia has a troubled regulatory track record: several large KSPs (Indosurya IDR 15T, Sejahtera Bersama) collapsed under fraudulent management, wiping out millions of member savings

**The opportunity this points to for PMA investors:**
The gap that KSP serves — small loans (IDR 1–50 juta) for UMKM that commercial banks won't serve — is precisely where fintech P2P lending (66191) is growing fastest. If you want to serve Bali's 500,000+ UMKM operators (warungs, craftsmen, villa support businesses), P2P lending under 66191 is the legal PMA path.

**Bali LPD note:** The Lembaga Perkreditan Desa is a village-level financial institution unique to Bali, governed by Perda Bali No. 3/2017 — it is NOT a koperasi and NOT governed by KBLI 64921. Foreign investment in LPDs is similarly not permitted.
